title: Zion is chastened but not moved from her place
setting: In late October and early November 1833, armed residents drove the Latter-day Saints out of Jackson County, Missouri. Two attackers died in a clash on 4 November, and a militia then disarmed the Saints. Most refugees crossed into Clay County, losing homes, goods, livestock, and crops. In Kirtland, Joseph Smith heard reports from Orson Hyde and John Gould and letters from Edward Partridge and others. Joseph dictated this revelation on 16–17 December 1833. The earliest known copy is undated; later copies give these dates.
summary: The revelation says the Lord allowed the affliction because of the Saints’ transgressions, naming contention, envy, and covetous desires. Yet it promises compassion and says the Lord will not cast them off. Zion will not be moved, and the pure in heart will return to build its waste places. It describes the day of the Lord’s coming, when enmity ends and all things are revealed. A parable tells of a nobleman’s servants who neglected to build a watchtower and lost the vineyard. The lord then sends a servant to gather the strength of his house and redeem it. The churches are to keep gathering, buy land in Jackson County, and not sell their claims there. The Saints are to petition the judge, the governor, and the president, under a Constitution the text says God established. Sidney Gilbert is told not to sell the storehouse.

contextNote.title: Stillness without explanation
contextNote.text: The exiled Saints wanted to know why they had suffered and how they would return. Joseph had written to them that the Lord’s only answer so far was to be still. Verse 16 repeats that counsel, and its reason is that “all flesh is in mine hands” already. Verse 17 joins this to a promise that Zion will not be moved out of her place. Verses 86–89 show that stillness did not mean doing nothing, since the Saints were to petition for redress. In this passage, being still means trusting God’s control while still acting lawfully.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson “Be Still and Know That I Am God” covers sections 98–101. It teaches that the Lord can comfort His people in trial. What reasons for hope do verses 9–18 give the scattered Saints?

newPeople.name: John Gould
newPeople.why: Setting; with Orson Hyde he reported the Jackson County violence to Joseph Smith on 25 November 1833. Also named in D&C 100:14.

reviewNote: Read all 101 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 16–17 December 1833, during the Missouri persecution, with most Saints in Clay County. JSP historical introduction read for the October–November violence, the 4 November deaths, the militia disarming the Saints, Joseph’s letters, and the earlier counsel to “be still.” JSP notes the earliest copy is undated. Liberty used to represent Clay County. JSP says it came to Joseph and Oliver Cowdery over one night, so Cowdery is included. Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary labeled verses 23–34 “the Millennium,” a term the text does not use, and omitted the parable’s second half (verses 55–62, the servant sent to redeem the vineyard). Both fixed.
